subject: Reliability bridge offer and conditional tier commitment
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@finano.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@finano.com>, Finano Ops <ops@finano.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes — upcoming renewal concerns

Lukas,

Thanks for taking this — we had another set of latency spikes during peak trading windows on Tue and Wed which materially impacted our ingestion pipeline. The attached usage-report-June.csv shows the request bursts and the increased tail latency. Our renewals team is pausing the commercial sign-off until we see a clear operational remediation or a stronger uptime commitment.

Two asks from Finano:
- A retroactive make-good for the incidents in June (we are asking for a one-month credit as a good-faith gesture).
- A firm SLO commitment for the next contract term (we are looking for 99.9% availability with defined operational runbooks).

We are open to a technical pilot, but it needs to be scoped and contractually represented if it is to factor into our renewal decision. Can we get an interim proposal this week?

Elena

Attachment: usage-report-June.csv (CSV, 74KB)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finano.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes — upcoming renewal concerns

Elena — thanks for the data and for flagging the renewal pause. I’m really sorry for the disruption; we own this. I’ve looped in Neha and Kim from our commercial team and Markus from Reliability so we can move quickly.

Short plan (today):
1) Immediate triage: Markus will run a deep-dive on the traces and KV cache behavior you attached and follow up by Friday with root-cause candidates.
2) Bridge offer: commercial proposal for an interim SLA uplift and a conditional commitment to a dedicated-capacity pilot that would (a) provide 99.9% SLO for the pilot workload and (b) include a one-time operational credit if we miss agreed SLOs during the pilot window.
3) Credit conversation: we’ll propose a partial credit for June as an interim gesture while we complete RCA.

I’ll get a draft of the bridge offer and a short statement of work for a 90-day dedicated pilot over to you by Monday. Can you confirm who on your legal/procurement side we should copy for contract turnaround?

— Lukas

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@finano.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes — upcoming renewal concerns

Elena — preliminary notes from our quick pass on the traces:
- We saw a correlated increase in tail latency when prefix cache miss rates rose during the 14:00–15:30 UTC window on June 9 and June 21.
- The serving nodes experienced a micro-burst of concurrent requests that exceeded our autoscale burst window; some requests fell back to a slower execution path.
- Short-term mitigations: we can provision a dedicated inference pool for your critical endpoints (isolated KV cache + tighter autoscale thresholds) to reduce contention.

Operational offer (what we can commit to in a bridge document):
- 90-day dedicated pilot with isolated capacity for the specified endpoints.
- Target SLO for pilot: 99.9% availability measured at the route-level, with agreed measurement windows and sample counts.
- Weekly operations review (30 minutes) during the pilot plus on-call escalation for Sev1s.
- If we miss the SLO during the pilot, an automatic credit equal to X% of monthly invoicing for each missed month (cap to be defined in contract).

We will attach a draft technical appendix and runbook to the bridge offer so your ops team can validate the measurement definitions.

— Markus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finano.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:51:00 -0400
Subject: Re: reliability bridge offer and conditional tier commitment

Elena — appreciate the candid ask. We’ve drafted a Bridge Offer that balances immediate commercial remediation with a clear operational path to sustained reliability. Key commercial points in the draft (attached):
- One-time invoice credit for June incidents: 25% of June recurring charges applied as a credit on your next invoice.
- Conditional tier commitment: if Finano signs the 90-day dedicated pilot and validates stability against the runbook, we’ll commit to an elevated SLA (contract amendment) for the next renewal term at a mutually agreed price.
- Pilot billing: the pilot will be billed at a reduced dedicated rate to account for the initial stabilization work.

We deliberately did not commit to a full-month credit greater than 25% upfront because we believe the pilot + operational guarantees provide faster, more durable remediation. That said, the draft includes an expedited execution clause: if we fail to reach the defined runbook goals within 45 days, the contract provides for an escalated credit path.

Can you share Finano’s acceptance threshold on the credit size and whether a 90-day pilot with these contractual guardrails would be acceptable to unlock renewal progress?

Attachment: SLA-Bridge-Offer-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Elena Rossi <elena@finano.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@finano.com>, Finano Ops <ops@finano.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: reliability bridge offer and conditional tier commitment

Kimberly / Lukas — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the constructive offer. Two quick replies from Finano:
1) The 25% one-time credit is a good-faith start; procurement wants to see a stronger downside if the pilot fails early — specifically they’d like the 45-day trigger to provide a 50% credit if runbook goals aren’t met.
2) Ops will review the technical appendix. If the runbook has measurable checks for prefix cache behavior and autoscale thresholds, they are inclined to move forward with the 90-day pilot.

If Redwood can accept the escalated-credit trigger (45 days -> 50% credit), Finano will sign the pilot statement of work and we’ll begin contract execution next week. Please send the final SOW and the updated bridge offer PDF with redlines today if possible; legal is standing by.

Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Reliability, Finano
